title: Commit FM configuration
description: Schema for commitfm.json, the control surface a human writes once and an agent may edit afterwards (the broadcast object only). Unknown top level keys are ignored rather than rejected, so a config written for a newer renderer still validates here, and an older renderer still accepts a config written by a newer one.

user.description: The GitHub login whose public activity drives derived mode: push events, repo descriptions and languages, and, only if the user opted in on their own profile, private contribution counts.

style.description: Which of the seven pure render style modules draws the banner. Each id names a src/styles/<id>.mjs module; an id outside this list has no matching renderer.

theme.description: Color scheme for the rendered banner. auto is resolved to light or dark before a style module ever sees the state, so no individual style module has to implement its own auto detection.

exclude.description: Repo names to hide from the banner entirely. Applied last, after every other selection rule such as pinning and rotation, and matches repo names exactly.

pin.description: Repo names to force into the rotation ahead of freshness ordering, so a repo the user cares about keeps showing even when it is not the most recently active one.

broadcast.description: An optional, time boxed override that lets an agent announce current work instead of the banner showing only derived GitHub activity. Absent means pure derived mode. A broadcast whose at plus ttlMinutes has already elapsed is ignored and the banner falls back to derived, so a forgotten note can never claim indefinitely that work is still happening.

repo.description: Name of the repo the broadcast note is about, shown alongside the note so the banner reads as this repo, this note rather than an unattributed status line.

note.description: Free text describing current work, for example refactoring the hook dispatcher. Attacker or agent influenced: always passed through sanitize.mjs before it becomes SVG text, regardless of what this schema allows through.

by.description: Identifier of whoever wrote the note, typically an agent id such as claude-opus-5. Empty or absent means the note's author is not tracked.

at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp of when the note was written. Combined with ttlMinutes this determines whether the broadcast is still fresh enough to show.

ttlMinutes.description: How many minutes after at the broadcast stays live before the renderer treats it as stale and falls back to derived mode. Defaults to 90 and is clamped to the 1 through 1440 range, one day, so a mistyped value cannot pin a stale note in place indefinitely or expire it in the past.
